name: Paris

French.commander: King Joseph, with Marshals Marmont and Mortier

summary: The allied armies attacked the heights of Belleville, Romainville and Montmartre, held by Marmont and Mortier with conscripts, National Guards and the pupils of the École Polytechnique; that night Marmont signed the capitulation, and the allies entered the city next day.

forces.name: Arrighi's Division
forces.summary: Lucotte's brigade of depot and veteran battalions, which held Montreuil and covered Bagnolet on the Malassise plateau on Marmont's right; the Russians took Montreuil and Bagnolet as the day went on.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Paris at seven in the morning of the 30th, from Koch's and Rapetti's histories and the French archives; most of its strengths are of early April.

The brigade had 1,250 men. The 1st Veteran Battalion had over six hundred; the other battalions a few dozen to a hundred and sixty. They are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit most of them.
The veteran battalions are shown as Line.
Nine battalions in one brigade, where the list's takes three regiments, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Ricard's Division
forces.summary: Marmont's reserve, massed by battalions before the Tourelles ridge behind the line from Romainville to Belleville.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Paris at seven in the morning of the 30th, from Koch's and Rapetti's histories and the French archives; most of its strengths are of early April.
The division had 726 men in seven battalions. Its battalions had a few dozen to a couple of hundred men each; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
Nafziger lists the 6th Léger in both brigades; it is shown once, with Pelleport's.
A brigade of four regiments, where the list's takes three, and two light regiments, where it allows one in the division, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Lagrange's Division
forces.summary: Marmont's centre, its two brigades either side of the road from Belleville to Romainville, holding the heights against Raevsky's Russians until Marmont asked for terms in the afternoon.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Paris at seven in the morning of the 30th, from Koch's and Rapetti's histories and the French archives; most of its strengths are of early April.
Its marine regiments were sailors and naval gunners of the fleet's artillery, brought inland in 1813; they fought well, and are shown as Line, the list's Veteran upgrade would suit them.
The division had 1,395 men. Its battalions had a few dozen to a couple of hundred men each; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
Nafziger gives the regiments without their battalions; the marine regiments' are those of his 12 March return, and the others are one battalion each.

Brigades of seven and six regiments, where the list's take three, fifteen battalions in Fournier's, where it takes ten, and two light regiments, where it allows one in the division, show as historical departures. Nafziger gives the division no guns.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Bordesoulle's Cavalry
forces.summary: The remnant of the I Cavalry Corps, in a second line behind the road to Montreuil on Marmont's right.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Paris at seven in the morning of the 30th, from Koch's and Rapetti's histories and the French archives; most of its strengths are of early April.
Merlin's light division, 850 men, is Hubert's and Foissac-Latour's brigades; Bordesoulle's heavy division, 895 men, Thiry's and Laville's. Their strengths are of 5 April.

Each brigade was made up of squadrons from the depots of many regiments: Nafziger names their parent regiments but not their strengths. They are grouped here as one unit for each kind of horse in a brigade, or two where a brigade had many, as they were formed into provisional regiments.
Each detachment had a few dozen men, the 8th Chasseurs and 4th Cuirassiers over a hundred; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.

Two heavy cavalry brigades, where the list takes one, cuirassiers and dragoons in one brigade, and more heavy cavalry than its half of the army for corps support, show as historical departures. Nafziger gives the corps no guns.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Boyer de Rébeval's Division
forces.summary: Part deployed and part massed before the village of Pré-Saint-Gervais, on the left of Marmont's line, where the allied attacks on the plain came in.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Paris at seven in the morning of the 30th, from Koch's and Rapetti's histories and the French archives; most of its strengths are of early April.
Guye's brigade had 1,850 men. The National Guards of the Nord are shown as Line.

Its three foot batteries are one in its divisional artillery and two in its reserve, as the list takes them; with seven battalions, where the list wants eight for each reserve battery, the two show as a historical departure.
This is a different division from the one Nafziger gives Boyer de Rébeval at Craonne.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Charpentier's Division
forces.summary: Mortier's reserve on the left, massed at the foot of the Chaumont ridge behind the line from Pantin to La Villette.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Paris at seven in the morning of the 30th, from Koch's and Rapetti's histories and the French archives; most of its strengths are of early April.
Its regiments were newly raised that winter, largely of conscripts under a cadre of veterans; they are the list's Young Guard, as it rates them.
The division had 1,500 men, the regiments seventy-five to two hundred and seventy each; each is shown as one battalion at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
Nafziger names the first brigade's commander as Lagrange, from a return of 15 April; it is shown here without him.
Brigades of six and four regiments, where the list's take three, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Curial's Division
forces.summary: Bigarré's brigade, massed in reserve behind Pantin, ready to support Sécrétant's Guard depot battalions holding the village.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Paris at seven in the morning of the 30th, from Koch's and Rapetti's histories and the French archives; most of its strengths are of early April.
Its regiments were newly raised that winter, largely of conscripts under a cadre of veterans; they are the list's Young Guard, as it rates them.
Bigarré's brigade had 1,820 men. The third and second battalions of other regiments that served in it are grouped as one regiment here; each unit is shown at full size.
Six regiments in one brigade, where the list's takes three, and one of three battalions, where it takes two, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Christiani's Division
forces.summary: Gros's brigade of the Guard's fusiliers, flanqueurs and vélites, massed in reserve between La Villette and La Chapelle to support Robert's Guard depot battalions.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Paris at seven in the morning of the 30th, from Koch's and Rapetti's histories and the French archives; most of its strengths are of early April.

The brigade had 1,630 men. Nafziger gives all six of its corps in one brigade under Gros; they are brigaded here as at Laon, the fusiliers and the flanqueurs, with the vélites as the list's Italian brigade. Each regiment has two battalions, as at Montmirail.
The Flanqueurs-Chasseurs and Flanqueurs-Grenadiers are the list's Tirailleurs.
A fusilier brigade with no Young Guard regiment, which the list's brigade wants, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Roussel d'Hurbal's Dragoons
forces.summary: Belliard's dragoons on Mortier's far left, out on the plain between the road to Saint-Denis and the Maillot gate.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Paris at seven in the morning of the 30th, from Koch's and Rapetti's histories and the French archives; most of its strengths are of early April.
The division had 1,900 men, with two march regiments besides.
Its two horse batteries are one in its divisional artillery and one in its reserve, as the list takes them.

Two heavy cavalry brigades, where the list takes one, more heavy cavalry than its half of the army for corps support, and a cavalry force with no infantry, show as historical departures. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Yorck's Corps
forces.summary: Yorck's Prussians on Blücher's wing, which came down from the north and took La Villette.
notes: Built from Albion Triumphant's Prussian 1815 list, the nearest to 1814: its Prussian Infantry Brigade is the brigade of 1813 and 1814, the size of another army's division, with line, reserve and Landwehr battalions.
Nafziger has no allied order of battle for Paris; this is the corps as on his latest return of it, some weeks before, and much weaker by the 30th. This is his Laon return.
A Prussian brigade was the size of another army's division, so the whole corps is here. Take the brigades you want; each is a force in itself.

Battalions of different regiments that served together are grouped as a regiment, as the list takes them. Reserve battalions are the list's Musketeers; grenadier battalions are Musketeers with its Veteran upgrade.
Brigades of three regiments or more have a Subordinate Commander, named where the order of battle names the brigade's infantry commander.
After a month's fighting several brigades had been put together, and their weakest battalions into combined ones; each combined battalion is shown as one unit.

Nafziger gives the 2nd East Prussian's two battalions as one regiment; the one here is grouped with the Brandenburg regiment, as the list takes three regiments in a brigade. The East Prussian National Cavalry, a volunteer regiment, and the Silesian Landwehr cavalry are the list's Mounted Landwehr.
Schmidt's corps artillery is the list's reserve, with a horse battery with each cavalry brigade.
More cavalry, reserve artillery and Schützen than the list allows for the corps' brigades, regiments of more battalions than it takes, and brigades without Landwehr, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Kleist's Corps
forces.summary: Kleist's Prussians beside Yorck's, which stormed La Chapelle.
notes: Built from Albion Triumphant's Prussian 1815 list, the nearest to 1814: its Prussian Infantry Brigade is the brigade of 1813 and 1814, the size of another army's division, with line, reserve and Landwehr battalions.
Nafziger has no allied order of battle for Paris; this is the corps as on his latest return of it, some weeks before, and much weaker by the 30th. This is his Laon return.
A Prussian brigade was the size of another army's division, so the whole corps is here. Take the brigades you want; each is a force in itself.

Battalions of different regiments that served together are grouped as a regiment, as the list takes them. Reserve battalions are the list's Musketeers; grenadier battalions are Musketeers with its Veteran upgrade.
Brigades of three regiments or more have a Subordinate Commander, named where the order of battle names the brigade's infantry commander.
After a month's fighting several brigades had been put together, and their weakest battalions into combined ones; each combined battalion is shown as one unit.

Nafziger gives only the 9th and 10th Brigades; the 11th and 12th, broken at Vauchamps, are not on his return. The 6th Reserve's third battalion was at Erfurt. The 10th Brigade's three combined battalions aren't named.

Zieten's cuirassiers and dragoons are the list's Dragoons, its only heavy cavalry; his light regiments are a brigade of their own here. The Silesian National Cavalry and Landwehr cavalry are the list's Mounted Landwehr.
Braun's corps artillery is the list's reserve, with a horse battery with each regular cavalry brigade.
More cavalry, reserve artillery and Schützen than the list allows for the corps' brigades, regiments of more battalions than it takes, and brigades without Landwehr, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Vorontsov's First Line
forces.summary: Vorontsov's corps, fifteen thousand infantry on Blücher's wing; its first line, with Benckendorff's horse.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
Nafziger has no allied order of battle for Paris; this is the corps as on his latest return of it, some weeks before, and much weaker by the 30th. This is his Craonne return.
Vorontsov, one of the list's named commanders, leads it; his corps is split here by its lines, as Nafziger gives it.
Benckendorff's detachment had a thousand men, Krasovsky's brigade 1,250 and Harpe's 2,154; each regiment is shown at full size.
Nafziger lists the Navaginsk regiment both here and in Poncet's division; it is shown in both, as he gives it.
Two light batteries and a position battery with seven battalions, where the list allows one light battery and no position battery, show as historical departures.

Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Major General Mikhail Vorontsov, with his own rating; but 2 of the 3 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Vuich's Corps
forces.summary: Vuich's corps of Vorontsov's, on Blücher's wing.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
Nafziger has no allied order of battle for Paris; this is the corps as on his latest return of it, some weeks before, and much weaker by the 30th. This is his Craonne return.
Swarikin's 24th Division (the first two brigades) and Poncet's 14th; the 19th Jäger are a brigade of their own here, as the list takes Jäger.
Its regiments had one or two battalions each, a few hundred men; each is shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them.
A Jäger brigade of one regiment, where the list wants two, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 2 of the 3 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Laptev's Division
forces.summary: Laptev's division of Vorontsov's corps, on Blücher's wing.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
Nafziger has no allied order of battle for Paris; this is the corps as on his latest return of it, some weeks before, and much weaker by the 30th. This is his Craonne return.
Nafziger gives the division's six regiments without brigades; they are brigaded here in pairs, in his order, with one of its batteries each.
Its regiments had one or two battalions each, a few hundred men; each is shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them.
Two light batteries and a position battery with six battalions, where the list allows one light battery and no position battery, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 2 of the 3 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Stroganov's Third Line
forces.summary: Stroganov's divisions of Vorontsov's corps, on Blücher's wing.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
Nafziger has no allied order of battle for Paris; this is the corps as on his latest return of it, some weeks before, and much weaker by the 30th. This is his Craonne return.

Stroganov, one of the list's named commanders, leads it. Khovansky's division had 1,800 men and Zheltukhin's 3,300; Nafziger gives Zheltukhin's only two regiments and its three batteries, and Khovansky's regiments without brigades, brigaded here in pairs.
Its regiments had one or two battalions each, a few hundred men; each is shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them.
Two light batteries in Zheltukhin's brigade, where the list allows one, show as a historical departure.

Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Major General Pavel Stroganov, with his own rating; but 2 of the 4 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: The Crown Prince of Württemberg's Corps
forces.summary: The Crown Prince's corps on the allied left, which with the Austrian grenadiers took the bridges of Saint-Maur and Charenton and Saint-Mandé.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Württemberg 1812 list, the nearest to 1814; Württemberg had joined the allies in November.
Nafziger has no allied order of battle for Paris; this is the corps as on his latest return of it, some weeks before, and much weaker by the 30th. This is his return of 15 February.

Koch's infantry is Döring's and Hohenlohe-Kirchberg's brigades, and Stockmayer's light brigade was with the advance guard. The horse chasseur regiments are the list's Jäger zu Pferde, and the Crown Prince's dragoons its Chevau-légers.
Each foot battery, four 6-pdrs and two howitzers, is the list's Light Artillery.
The Archduke Ferdinand Hussars, Austrians with the advance guard, are with Schäffer's brigade; an Austrian pioneer company is left out.

Two cavalry brigades, where the list allows one for the infantry, two Jäger zu Pferde regiments in Jett's brigade, where it takes one, and three regiments in Döring's brigade and four light battalions in Stockmayer's, where the list's take two, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Gyulai's Corps
forces.summary: Gyulai's Austrians on the allied left, sent against the forest of Vincennes.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Austrian 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
Nafziger has no allied order of battle for Paris; this is the corps as on his latest return of it, some weeks before, and much weaker by the 30th. This is Wikipedia's La Rothière order of battle.

Crenneville's light division is Haecht's and Trenck's brigades, Fresnel's Pflüger's and Csollich's, and Prince Hohenlohe's Splény's and Grimmer's. The St George Grenz regiment's two battalions are one with each of Crenneville's brigades.
The Mariassy and Ignaz Gyulai regiments, recruited in Hungary, are the list's Hungarian infantry.

Regiments of three and four battalions, where the list takes two Large ones, two advanced guard brigades, where it allows one, and four brigade batteries and two position batteries, where it allows three and one, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Gorchakov's Corps
forces.summary: Gorchakov's infantry of Raevsky's corps, which took Montreuil.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
After Nafziger's return of the Army of Bohemia in January 1814; the corps was much weaker by the time of this battle.

Mezentsov's 5th Division (the first three brigades) and Helfreich's 14th (the last three), with a light and a position battery. Nafziger's Craonne and Laon returns give the Tula and Navaginsk regiments to Vorontsov's corps in March.
Four infantry brigades and two Jäger brigades, where the list allows three and one, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 3 of the 6 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Eugen of Württemberg's Corps
forces.summary: Eugen of Württemberg's infantry of Raevsky's corps, in the attack on the heights of Romainville.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
After Nafziger's return of the Army of Bohemia in January 1814; the corps was much weaker by the time of this battle.

Prince Eugen of Württemberg, one of the list's named commanders, leads it. Shakhovsky's 3rd Division (the first three brigades) and Pyshnitsky's 4th (the last three), with a light and a position battery; the 4th Division's Jäger brigade has no named commander.
Four infantry brigades and two Jäger brigades, where the list allows three and one, show as historical departures.

Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Major General Eugene von Württemberg, with his own rating; but 3 of the 6 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Pahlen's Cavalry
forces.summary: Pahlen's horse, with Raevsky's corps on the allied centre.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
After Nafziger's return of the Army of Bohemia in January 1814; the corps was much weaker by the time of this battle.
Three light cavalry brigades, where the list allows one, and cavalry with no infantry brigade to allow it, show as historical departures.

toCome.name: Compans's and Ledru des Essarts's Divisions
toCome.summary: Chabert's brigade, 2,200 men, in skirmish order in the Romainville woods, and Bongars's, 1,600, on the Beauregard ridge; Nafziger doesn't know their battalions.

toCome.name: Chastel's Cavalry
toCome.summary: Vincent's brigade, 1,600 horse, in line between Charonne and Montreuil; its regiments aren't known.

toCome.name: Michel's Guard Depots
toCome.summary: Four thousand men from the Guard's depots, Sécrétant's brigade behind Pantin and Robert's before Aubervilliers.

toCome.name: Belliard's Other Cavalry and Ornano's
toCome.summary: Ghigny's, Christophe's and Leclerc's brigades, along the old entrenchments between the road to Saint-Denis and the Maillot gate, and Dautencourt's 320 Guard horse on the far left; their regiments aren't known.

toCome.name: Moncey's National Guard
toCome.summary: Some six thousand National Guards on the heights from Montmartre round to the Bercy, with 780 gunners of veteran battalions and the École Polytechnique on the city walls, and naval gunners serving the batteries at Pré-Saint-Gervais.

toCome.name: The Russian Guard and Reserve
toCome.summary: Yermolov's Guard came up late; the Russians took Bagnolet and Charonne.

toCome.name: The Prussian Guard
toCome.summary: Thrown back at Pantin, then took the French guns there.

toCome.name: Langeron's Corps
toCome.summary: Came on by Le Bourget on Blücher's wing.

toCome.name: The Austrian Grenadiers
